findings.description: General letter (line 39) claims the ICESCR 'has never received a committee hearing' and Dear Colleague letter (line 167) claims 'no committee hearing.' Both contradict the site's own account in icescr-at-fifty.md (line 36: 'The Senate Foreign Relations Committee held hearings in 1979') and the glossary entry for 'ratification' ('committee hearings occurred in 1979'). Internal consistency requires correcting the template letters to acknowledge the 1979 hearings.
findings.suggestion: Change 'never received a committee hearing, a committee vote, or a floor vote' to 'received committee hearings in 1979 but never a committee vote or floor vote' in both the General Letter and Dear Colleague Letter templates.
findings.context: General Letter: 'In the 49 years since, the treaty has never received a committee hearing, a committee vote, or a floor vote.' | Dear Colleague: 'In 49 years, the treaty has received no committee hearing, no committee vote, and no floor vote.'

findings.description: The Article 6 talking point cites 'A projected loss of 550,000 jobs' without attribution. The same figure appears in template-letters.mdx line 91 ('Trade policy changes project 550,000 fewer jobs by end of 2026') also without a source link. Other statistics on the same pages carry citations (OBBBA figures cite CBO/KFF). An unattributed projection in advocacy material weakens credibility.
findings.suggestion: Add the source for the 550,000 jobs projection — link to the originating analysis or data source (CBO, BLS, or the site's own evidence page).
findings.context: talking-points.mdx: 'A projected loss of 550,000 jobs — without a government strategy to absorb the displacement — should alarm every constituent.' | template-letters.mdx: 'Trade policy changes project 550,000 fewer jobs by end of 2026.'

findings.description: Researcher letter cites 'The productivity-pay gap has widened by a factor of 3.5 since 1979 (Economic Policy Institute)' with a named source but no URL. Other letters in the same file cite sources with direct URLs (UN Treaty Collection, OHCHR). The voter-guide-rights-inventory post provides the URL (https://www.epi.org/productivity-pay-gap/) for the same data source. Consistency warrants adding the link here too.
findings.suggestion: Change '(Economic Policy Institute)' to '([Economic Policy Institute](https://www.epi.org/productivity-pay-gap/))' to match the citation pattern used in other letters and in the voter guide.
findings.context: Researcher letter: 'The productivity-pay gap has widened by a factor of 3.5 since 1979 (Economic Policy Institute). AI adoption accelerates this divergence structurally...'
